title: Create per-model compile manifests and staged kernel heuristics for conditional-expert topologies
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: We need a safe, auditable, and model-specific way to publish compilation artifacts and kernel selection heuristics for models with conditional execution (MoE, GQA) and multi-head attention variants. Current publish flows bake a single 'best' kernel profile per model binary which lacks per-shard/route sensitivity and makes rollbacks coarse-grained.

Goal: Define and implement a versioned compile manifest format that expresses: staged compile artifacts, per-route/kernel candidates, confidence scores, hardware applicability, allowed fallbacks, and explicit rollback hooks. Implement the service-side orchestration for publishing manifests, running staged canaries, collecting telemetry, and automated rollback when SLO regressions are detected.

Scope: MVP covers: 1) manifest schema design; 2) tool to produce manifests from compilation runs (including multi-profile outputs for MHA/GQA/MoE topologies); 3) publish + activate flow in the model-onboarder with staged weights (canary 1%, 10%, 100%); 4) telemetry hooks to capture per-route latency/cost/quality; 5) rollback automation on threshold breaches. Exclusions: automatic recompilation on failure, and cross-customer shared profile publishing (future work).
acceptance_criteria: A stable JSON/YAML manifest schema exists and is documented (fields: manifest_id, model_version, compile_date, artifacts:list, route_profiles:list, hardware_targets:list, confidence_score, fallback_order, signature)
Onboarder can ingest a multi-artifact manifest and register all artifacts under a single model_version with strict immutability semantics
Console shows staged activation status and canary weight; ops can adjust weights and force-rollback
Per-route telemetry (p50/p95 latency, failure rate, token-cost delta, quality regression metric) is emitted and stored for canary windows
Automated rollback triggers on configurable SLO regressions (latency + failure-rate OR quality drop) and reverts routing to previous manifest within the defined SLA
Integration tests simulate MoE/GQA request paths and validate that correct artifact is selected per route and that fallback semantics are honored
tasks: Design manifest schema and write spec (including signature and immutability policy)
Extend compile pipeline to emit multi-profile artifacts and a manifest generator tool
Add model-onboarder endpoints: publish-manifest, activate-manifest, set-canary-weight
Wire telemetry: route tag propagation, per-artifact metrics aggregation, and dashboard panels
Implement canary controller: gradual weight adjustment, health checks, and rollback logic
Create integration test harness for MoE/GQA topologies with synthetic workload and golden quality signals
Document rollout runbook and add Console UI hooks for visibility and manual controls
decisions: Use a manifest-first approach instead of editing model binary metadata to keep artifacts immutable and auditable
Represent per-route kernels as ordered candidate lists with confidence scores to allow soft selection and safe fallbacks
Canary cadence: initial 1% for 30 minutes, 10% for 2 hours, then 100% if no regressions detected (configurable per-model)
Rollback policy: trigger when p95 latency increases >25% AND error rate increases >1% over baseline, or when quality evaluation metric drops >2%
